title: Landscape-first continuation map for all nine research lanes

method.landscape_ledger: Records new correspondences, classifications, calculational tools, model examples, obstructions and experimentally meaningful analogues even when they do not close the full programme.
method.closure_ledger: Separately records whether a result selects physical sources, normalization, orientation, dynamics or a non-generic observable.
method.continuation_rule: A lane is continued while it has a technically plausible next bridge and a bounded calculation capable of changing what is known. Genericity lowers ontological weight but does not erase exploratory value.
method.stopping_rule: Pause a lane only when its next bridge requires an undefined object, repeats an already classified equivalence, or has no conceivable calculation that distinguishes its alternatives.

lanes.landscape_question: Which physically implementable probe pairs generate different two-channel quotients of the Standard Model, and how are those quotients related?
lanes.landscape_value: Builds an operational taxonomy of source frames and may reveal that several apparently competing algebraic carriers correspond to different laboratory protocols.
continuations: Catalogue gauge-invariant source protocols: background B-L field, Higgs-modulated incidence insertion, stress/strain probes and flavor-tagged weak processes.
Calculate how calibration, contact subtraction and source shear act on measurable ratios for each protocol.
Compare the protocols by Fisher information or response tomography to determine which combinations are experimentally identifiable.
lanes.decision_test: Construct two explicit source protocols and determine whether their normalized cross-response distinguishes the two topology assignments after all calibration freedoms are quotiented.
lanes.go_signal: A protocol selects a reproducible frame or measures an orientation-sensitive invariant.
lanes.no_go_signal: Every candidate observable is related by unconstrained source recalibration and no operational quotient distinguishes the assignments.

lanes.landscape_question: What is the smallest renormalization-closed module containing incidence and B-L?
lanes.landscape_value: Even if it is larger than two dimensions, the answer identifies the natural dynamical carrier and shows how the Jordan two-channel picture sits inside it.
continuations: Retain the completed Higgs-plus-fermion quotient and its exact Yukawa/anomaly kernels as the source-space baseline.
Retain the exact five-coordinate quotient obtained after the completed Higgs, hypercharge-EOM, anomaly and B-L reductions.

Use the verified rank-four visible map to design bottom and weak-anomaly measurements with interference information, while treating the light-neutrino coordinate as practically null in the low-mass regime.
lanes.decision_test: Determine whether a physical metric uniquely fixes an incidence-family ray and whether the resolved part of that ray survives nuisance profiling; in parallel determine whether the direct vector-source module has a stable quotient.
lanes.go_signal: A physical contraction uniquely fixes the ALP relative-charge ray, its accessible coordinates are experimentally identifiable, or a stable direct-current quotient emerges.
lanes.no_go_signal: The incidence normalization remains conventional, ordinary ALP nuisance directions reproduce all accessible correlations and the direct source plane remains scheme-dependent.

lanes.landscape_question: Which parts of the response geometry survive a regulator, finite volume, interactions and continuum extrapolation?
lanes.landscape_value: Separates exact continuum principles from artifacts of Gaussian or finite-dimensional models and provides nonperturbative spectral data.
continuations: Implement the anomaly-free generation in a small domain-wall or overlap-fermion lattice model.
Measure the Euclidean 2x2 correlator, Ward residuals, mirror contamination and eigenframe drift under changes of lattice spacing.
Use positive spectral reconstruction or functional methods to compare continuum moments with the analytic UV metric.
lanes.decision_test: Perform a controlled refinement study of the response rank, normalized off-diagonal coherence and source eigenvectors.
lanes.go_signal: A regulator-independent carrier or unexpected protected relation survives extrapolation.
lanes.no_go_signal: The distinctive structure disappears with refinement or depends on mirror/regulator choices.

lanes.landscape_question: Can chirality, orientation and response be different boundary shadows of one bulk construction?
lanes.landscape_value: Organizes anomaly inflow, domain-wall chirality, mirror removal and orientation in one geometric setting even if no unique bulk is selected.
continuations: Complete the finite-slab spectrum and inflow ledger for one anomaly-free generation with gauge links.
Classify allowed mirror-gapping interactions and boundary counterterms under the exact gauge symmetries.
Compute whether reversal of the wall normal induces the established orientation-odd response.
lanes.decision_test: Construct one finite bulk-boundary model and simultaneously check anomaly inflow, mirror gap, boundary Ward identities and orientation reversal.
lanes.go_signal: The same bulk datum fixes chirality and the measurable response orientation.
lanes.no_go_signal: Mirror removal or orientation requires independent boundary choices, leaving the bulk explanation nonselective.

lanes.landscape_question: Which spectral-triple or superconnection axioms are compatible with the audited Furey matter TRO and its unique allowed pairings?
lanes.landscape_value: Provides a systematic comparison between Furey matter geometry and action-generating noncommutative geometry, including precise incompatibility results.
continuations: Retain the verified doubled Furey-arrow Hilbert space, grading and real structure that repairs the four desired Dirac Yukawa links.
Retain the verified gauge-dressed split in which colour-linearity leaves the four desired Yukawa links while coloured finite fluctuations produce optional S1/S3 leptoquark channels.

Construct a broken exceptional/Furey action that reconciles the exceptional ten with the Furey first-order removal of its two diquark channels, then classify the remaining Majorana-orientability fork.
lanes.decision_test: Determine whether gauge dressing removes exactly the three extra doubled-arrow links while preserving the four desired Dirac channels, and whether a sterile Majorana term can coexist with an acceptable orientability condition.
lanes.go_signal: The completed bimodule and gauge algebra reduce the seven formal links to the observed four, or force a sharply testable additional scalar sector.
lanes.no_go_signal: All seven links remain arbitrary and the Majorana-orientability choice can only be made by unrestricted finite-Dirac input.

lanes.landscape_question: How does the two-current and orientation structure constrain allowed form factors and amplitudes?
lanes.landscape_value: Translates the programme into on-shell language, reveals which relations are generic consequences of unitarity, and identifies observables requiring new dynamics.
continuations: Use the absorptive spectral matrix, rather than contact-sensitive Euclidean coefficients, to define fixed-energy broken-current directions.
Carry the scale-free production-BR-times-lifetime discriminator through exact kaon and B experimental acceptances in the reduced five-coordinate quotient.
Fit the presently accessible top-lepton slice and quantify the improvement required from radiative Upsilon decay or another bottom-sensitive channel to close the remaining fermionic direction.
lanes.decision_test: Fit rare-meson production together with displaced or invisible decay information at fixed ALP mass and test which fermion-charge coordinates are distinguishable without knowing the overall scale, explicitly leaving the bottom coordinate unclaimed unless a bottom-sensitive observable reaches it.
lanes.go_signal: The production-times-lifetime correlation separates the accessible incidence-family slice from standard same-top-coupling benchmarks, with a plausible route to bottom sensitivity.
lanes.no_go_signal: Detector acceptance or independent EFT coefficients continuously reproduce the accessible correlation, or bottom sensitivity remains parametrically disconnected from the kaon reach.

lanes.landscape_question: Can a state and inclusion select the real structure and direction of response that the finite algebra leaves free?
lanes.landscape_value: Tests the idea that orientation and reality belong to algebra-plus-state rather than algebra alone and clarifies links between KMS, modular flow and source/response duality.
continuations: Construct a finite standard-pair toy model reproducing the two-channel cone and calculate its modular conjugation explicitly.
Replace it by a free-field local algebra with the chosen vacuum or KMS state and identify the induced conditional expectation.
Compare modular reversal with CP, face exchange and physical time reversal on the Standard-Model operators.
lanes.decision_test: Vary the faithful state and test whether the selected real form and orientation remain invariant under all states compatible with the same physical preparation.
lanes.go_signal: A physically specified state/inclusion uniquely induces the required selector and reversal.
lanes.no_go_signal: The modular data rotate continuously with arbitrary state choices and have no stable Standard-Model interpretation.

lanes.landscape_question: Which defect, pump or mixed frequency-space domains support the orientation information excluded from pure passive frequency winding?
lanes.landscape_value: Classifies where the existing topological indices are meaningful and connects abstract selector winding to boundary modes and transport.
continuations: Construct the mixed frequency-defect family with its full compactification, poles, zeros and gap conditions.
Compute the index analytically and in the finite-range lattice representative.
Couple the defect coordinate to a physical Higgs, wall or flux texture and derive its response coefficient.
lanes.decision_test: Test whether the mixed invariant forces a protected zero mode or quantized orientation-odd transport when the defect is generated by a local action.
lanes.go_signal: A robust boundary state or transport signature survives symmetry-preserving deformations.
lanes.no_go_signal: The invariant vanishes on the correct domain or relies on an externally drawn coordinate with no physical field.

lanes.landscape_question: Which aspects of the programme are universal collective-response phenomena, and which require the Standard-Model/Furey microstructure?
lanes.landscape_value: Creates tangible analogues, exposes universality classes and may reveal the correct effective rather than microscopic interpretation of Spin(2,3).
continuations: Build a reciprocal mechanical or acoustic two-port realizing the positive Jordan cone and controlled orientation reversal.
Add the minimal nonreciprocal or defect coupling needed to reproduce the odd witness.
Compare its invariants with the Standard-Model source and topology routes to isolate microstructure-sensitive data.
lanes.decision_test: Measure whether two devices with identical H2(R) static cones but different coupling graphs can be distinguished by the proposed dynamical observable.
lanes.go_signal: The experiment identifies a response feature that tracks the special graph or orientation rather than the cone alone.
lanes.no_go_signal: All proposed signatures depend only on generic reciprocal two-port theory.
